title: WPMS/43/2023 of HABIBUR REHMAN Vs MUSSOORIE DEHRADUN DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY

paras.text:
1
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (M/S) No. 43 of 2023
Habibur Rehman ..................Petitioner

-Versus-Mussoorie Dehradun Development Authority & Others
 ..............Respondents
Present: Mr. Aditya Singh, the learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. Suyash Pant, learned Standing Counsel for the State.
Mr. Rahul Consul, learned counsel for the MDDA.
Date of Hearing and Order: 09.01.2023
Sri Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.
Upon hearing the learned counsel for the parties, the Court has
passed the following order:-
1. By filing this writ petition, the petitioner has prayed for
the following reliefs:-
a. Issue a writ order or direction, in the nature of
Certiorari quashing the impugned order dated
28.12.2022 passed by the learned Prescribed
Authority/S.D.M. Doiwala, District - Dehradun,
contained as Annexure No. 4 to the writ petition.
b. Issue a writ, order or direction, which this Hon'ble
Court may deem fit and proper under the facts and
circumstances of the case.

2
c. Award the cost of the petition.
2. It is not disputed at this stage that the petitioner does
not have a sanctioned map from the Mussoorie
Dehradun Development Authority for carrying out the
constructions, which is sought to be demolished by the
Development Authority.
3. It is brought to our notice that the construction that is
in dispute in this case is a temporary tin structure built
upon iron angles and iron rods and it is being used as a
commercial place for washing cars/vehicles.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that
as per the definition provided in the Uttarakhand Urban
& Country Planning and Development Act, 1973,
(hereinafter referred to as "the Development Act" for
brevity), the temporary structure is not a building.
However, in reference to Clause (b) of Section 2 of the
Development Act reveals that building includes any
structure or erection or part of a structure or erection
which is intended to be used for residential, industrial,
commercial or other purposes, whether in actual use or
not.

3
5. Thus, it is clear that the Act itself does not make a
distinction between permanent structures and
temporary structures. The Clause (e) provides for the
definition of 'Development', which includes with all its
grammatical variations, means the carrying out of
building, engineering, mining or other operations in, on,
over or under land, or the making of any material
change in any building or land, and includes re-development.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner relying upon the
Building Byelaws of Uttarakhand would draw the
attention of the Court to Paragraph 2.11, which provides
the definition of "Building". Building shall mean any
structure for whatsoever purpose and of whatsoever
materials constructed and every part thereof, whether
used as human habitation or not including foundation,
plinth, walls, floors, roofs, chimneys, plumbing and
building services, fixed platforms, veranda, balcony,
cornice or projection, part of a building or anything
affixed thereto,
A "Temporary building" has been defined as
temporary building shall mean a building built of un-

4
burnt bricks, burnt bricks without mortar, corrugated
iron, bamboo, thatch, wood boarding or plywood but
shall not include a building built of burnt bricks, cement
blocks or stones laid in mortar. These building Byelaws
have been formulated under the provisions of the Act.
So, any conflict between the provisions of the
Development Act and the provisions of the Byelaws, then
the Development Act shall take precedent because the
Act is passed by the Legislative Assembly, whereas the
Building Byelaws are delegated legislations.
7. In that view of the matter, this Court is of the opinion
that the contention of the learned counsel for the
petitioner is that it is not building is of no avail.
Admittedly, he do not have any sanctioned map to carry
out business there by constructing a temporary shed.
Hence, the writ petition is without merit. However, if the
State Government or the Development Authority wants
to use the land after removal of the unauthorized
structure thereon, then they must acquire it under the
relevant provisions of law and then use it for other
purposes.

5
8. With such observations, the writ petition is dismissed
being devoid of merit.
No order as to costs.
(Sanjaya Kumar Mishra, J.)
 09.01.2023
(Grant urgent certified copy of this order, as per Rules)
A/ -
